owner_decisions_issue.title: gate:owner — the 22 acts and decisions that stand between the platform and a full A (one issue, ordered by leverage per minute)
owner_decisions_issue.body:
Every gap across the 2026-09-05 review's 17 lenses that is NOT code and NOT money lands here. Nothing below is a story; each item is a decision only you can make or an act only you can perform. Total one-off attended time: **~6h 44m**, plus two standing behaviours. Filed stories and RCA process work are referenced by number and never re-proposed.

The honest headline first: **with the cost bound lifted to any number, and every free story landed, zero of the 17 lenses reaches a full A without something on this list.** The dollar cost of the entire plan is $2.67/mo gross, $1.37/mo net.

---

## Tier 0 — the one decision that moves twelve lenses

**1. Rule on reset cadence: a MINIMUM cycle length, not just a `--reanchor-of` guard.** (30 min · #3601)
Unblocks: qs, cpo, narrative, reader, aiq, dataviz, designer, observability, cto, growth, principal, data-architect.
Measured basis: 12 resets in 55 days; cycle lengths since 2026-07-12 are 1, 5, 1, 1, 2, 5, 7, 7, 7, 15, 4 days (median 5). Exactly one of those eleven cycles could have matured a 14-day pre-registered bet. At ≥14 days, dataviz and designer reach a full A and five more lenses become gradeable at all. At ≥30 days, four more reach A and the ops lenses stop fighting their own reset. Every other item on this list is measured in minutes; this one is measured in lenses.

---

## Tier 1 — under five minutes each, and something is currently broken in production

**2. Apply the tracked IAM JSON to the live role.** (2 min · #3562, closed-but-unapplied)
```
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name github-actions-remediation-role \
  --policy-name remediation-permissions \
  --policy-document file://infra/iam/github-actions-remediation-role.permissions.json
```
main has 24 Sids with SES scoped to `arn:aws:ses:us-west-2:205930651321:identity/mattsusername.com`. The LIVE role still has 20 Sids and 5 wildcards, including `ses:SendEmail`/`sesv2:SendEmail` Resource:* with no Condition and `logs:FilterLogEvents` Resource:* — the exact statements the review named. The fix merged at 06:28 PT and the issue closed at 13:28Z without ever reaching the role. This is the #3595 closure-on-merge class, live, on the security lens. Unblocks: security.

**3. Flip two GitHub repo settings.** (2 min · unfiled)
Settings → Code security: `secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns` and `secret_scanning_validity_checks` are both **disabled** today. Without them the platform's own bearer shapes — the MCP `lp_` prefix, the HAE ingest bearer, the Telegram secret-token, SITE_API_ORIGIN_SECRET — match no provider pattern and are invisible to both GitHub's scanner and gitleaks' default ruleset. And *live*, the word the security anchor actually uses, is exactly what validity checks decide. Both are free on a public repo. Unblocks: security.

**4. Confirm the urgent SNS topic has a live confirmed subscription** on a device you read in a no-session week, and say so on the record. (5 min · #3499)
#3499 routes reader-audience alarms there; routing an alarm to an unconfirmed topic is the F-anchor's "routed to nowhere" wearing a green check. Unblocks: cto, observability.

**5. Rule on the Dropbox capture channel.** (5 min · #3571)
Does `dropbox` join the #746 capture_channel set (hae/notion/mcp), or does macrofactor carry `capture_channel: None` with a dated reason? Honesty is preserved today (age is shown in hours); the platform's own "dark N days" standard is applied unevenly. Unblocks: integrations.

---

## Tier 2 — ten to twenty minutes each

**6. Publish the cycle-16 pre-registration.** (10 min · #3390 carries the runlist; the publish itself has no issue)
`publish_genesis_preregistration.py` + `genesis_prereg_stamp.py`. Verified live today: `/experiments/prereg/genesis-2026-09-05.json` → **404**, `.sha256.json` → **404**, while `genesis-2026-09-01.json` still 200s. The season's 14 predictions and 2 hypotheses are on nobody's record but DynamoDB's, and cycle 16 stays UNSEALED — needing a permanent grandfather record if it closes without one (cycle 13's precedent). Unblocks: qs.

**7. Rule on `freshness-interior-gap`.** (10 min · #3504)
In ALARM since 2026-08-31T08:02 PT — **5.1 days**, already past the anchor's 72h. Its citation contains an owner decision with no carrier issue: does an acknowledged-unfillable historical gap (Eight Sleep 2026-08-30, which never existed) suppress the alarm, or does the alarm stay honest and the source's #2643 absence marker land instead? #3504 assumes the second. Until you rule, the days keep accruing. Unblocks: cto, observability.

**8. Rule on the phase class of the protocol-lever registry.** (10 min · unfiled)
Are `PROTOCOL#` levers `experiment_scoped` (wiped to zero every cycle, as today — /api/protocols returns count=0 and the DDB query returns 0 items) or a `cross_phase` registry? This is a `phase_taxonomy.py` class decision, not a code choice, and it decides whether the qs anchor's lever clause can ever be non-vacuous. Unblocks: qs.

**9. Rule on where the incident corpus lives.** (10 min · unfiled)
225 `reference_*` topics sit in `~/.claude/projects/`, which no repo gate can read, while CLAUDE.md instructs agents to read the index before writing a gate — that instruction **is** the devex anchor's failing condition, stated as operating procedure. Either the gate becomes a hook that runs against the memory directory, or the gate-pointer half of each topic moves into the public repo. Only you can rule on private memory content entering a public repo. Unblocks: devex.

**10. Commit to a chronicle send weekday and a send count.** (10 min · #3564 closed the copy; the cadence is the residue)
The delivery day is currently an OUTPUT of `CHRONICLE_AUTOPUBLISH_HOURS=48`, so honest copy is necessarily hedged ("Wednesday, or Friday, when an unapproved draft auto-publishes") and no derivation test can pin it to a fixed cadence — because there is no fixed cadence to pin it to. Unblocks: growth, narrative.

**11. Reverse or re-affirm the 2026-08-02 #1991 branch-1 posture.** (10 min · #3547, closed won't-do)
Both per-deploy visual-QA invocations omit `--color-scheme`, so the gate runs in DARK only; light is compared on alternating ISO weeks and is advisory, meaning a light regression can be live for up to 14 days and does not block. The a11y anchor says "BOTH themes … with a gating audit", so as written it quietly asks a reviewer to overturn your decision. Name what evidence would change it, or let the anchor cite the posture. Unblocks: a11y.

**12. Rule on tap targets.** (15 min · #3547, closed won't-do — the decision box died with it)
Adopt WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24×24 as the hard floor — which means bucketing the home waveform's ~90 day-bars into ≥24px hit columns and flipping `tests/test_wave_tap_target.py`, which today asserts that ~2px-wide targets **pass** — or record the one-axis rule as the platform's standard in DESIGN_SYSTEM_V5 with the SC delta named and an issue carrying it. This trades a flagship visual against a published accessibility standard. Unblocks: a11y, designer.

**13. Authorize the tier-3 hard-cutoff drill.** (15 min · unfiled)
SSM `/life-platform/budget-tier` history shows values **0, 1 and 2 only** (tier 2 on 08-26 and 08-30, back to 0 on 08-31). Band 3 — the one that raises rather than degrades — has never once executed in production, on the platform's single most consequential fail-closed path. The drill sets tier 3 in a low-traffic window, hits /api/ask, /api/board_ask and one brief invoke, captures the paused responses and the `BudgetExceeded` raise, confirms `reader_truth_qa` and `visual_ai_qa` pause, restores 0. Bedrock spend during the drill is zero by construction; the cost is deliberately degrading the live reader surface for the window. Unblocks: cost.

**14. Remove or rewrite the 5 reader-input objects already public.** (15 min · #3559 moves the write site only)
